`proof/bounds` extends exact interval optimization to mixed-integer linear programs (branch-and-bound), integer and mixed-integer linear-fractional ratios (Dinkelbach iteration), and univariate quadratic and coupled bilinear (`x * y`) objectives (2D Fourier-Motzkin polygon projection, interior edge stationary points, and integer slicing).

`proof/bounds` computes exact tight `[min, max]` bounds and endpoint witnesses for integer linear-fractional ratios (via Dinkelbach) and coupled bilinear products (including interior edge stationary points).

Standard library adds `graph/influence` for exact cumulative weighted path propagation across arbitrary depth (topological DP on DAGs, cycle-avoiding simple-path enumeration on cyclic graphs) and `proof/sensitivity` for all-derivations epistemic fragility (`holds`, `critical`, `redundant`, `resilient`, `minCutSize`, `minimalCuts`).

`graph/influence` computes exact cumulative weighted path propagation over multi-hop graphs and `proof/sensitivity` computes exact single-point-of-failure facts and minimal cut sets across all derivations.

`proof/valid?` rejects forged `{check: true}` objects, verifies `proof/bounds` results directly, tightens `why` derivation checks, and accepts an optional second `claim` argument (`{"atLeast": ...}`, `{"above": ...}`, `{"atMost": ...}`, `{"below": ...}`, `{"min": ...}`, `{"max": ...}`, `{"unsat": true}`, relation name, or ground atom) for claim-bound verification.
`proof/valid?` rejects forged `{check: true}` objects, validates `proof/bounds` records directly, and checks optional 2-argument claim bindings.

Top-level `define` accepts an optional `{"persist": true}` fourth argument to save snapshot-writable helper bindings in the logic database across `--database` runs and snapshots, and `lion check` adds Lion-in-Lion lints for multi-goal `find`/`query` calls and bare logic variables in top-level `fact` forms.
`define` with `{"persist": true}` persists helper definitions across snapshots and database runs while leaving plain 3-argument `define` ephemeral.
